title: Prospective audit and feedback for antimicrobial stewardship: a two-strand scoping review of measured outcomes and experience of recommendations
abstract: Objective: to map measured outcomes of prospective audit and feedback (strand A) and experience of stewardship recommendations (strand B), with attention to surgery, intensive care and small hospitals. Design: scoping review following JBI guidance with a convergent segregated approach, reported with PRISMA-ScR. Results will be charted by March 2027.
introduction: Audit and feedback reduces antimicrobial use modestly, but results depend on how recommendations are delivered and received. A stewardship committee needs both kinds of evidence, kept separate, to decide how to extend the service.
methods: Searches by the network library; screening by a pharmacist with a second screener from January; strand A charted with 20 percent verification; strand B coded jointly with an infectious diseases fellow; joint display for surgery, intensive care and small hospitals. Certainty was not rated.
results: No charting has been done yet. The report will present the PRISMA-ScR flow diagram, the strand A evidence map, the strand B framework synthesis and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will set out what each strand says about extending the service with the same staff and where the evidence is silent.
limitations: English and French only; single screening early on; few small-hospital reports.
conclusion: To be written after charting; it will describe the evidence and will not estimate effects.
summary: PRISMA-ScR draft with results left empty until charting.
